test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 27 Mar 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question:
Supposing that the telegraph poles on a railroad are 50 m apart, how many poles will be passed by a train in 4 h if the speed of the train is 45 km/h?

(Include both the poles at the starting point as well as the one at the end of the journey in your count)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Total Distance** = Speed × Time = 45 km/h × 4 h = 180 km = 1,80,000 m.

**Number of Intervals** = Total Distance ÷ Distance between poles = 1,80,000 ÷ 50 = 3600.

**Total Poles** = Number of Intervals + 1 = 3600 + 1 = 3601.

**∴ The correct answer is 3601.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance between two **telegraph poles** = 50 m

**Speed** of the train = 45 km/h

**Time** taken = 4 h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2417bcbf453c775d6dc6c01e20aaf0691ee6121bce7c34602b464fa8ad3ca5db.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total distance** covered = Speed × Time

⇒ Total distance = 45 × 4 = 180 km

⇒ Converting km to meters: 180 × 1000 = 1,80,000 m

⇒ Number of **gaps** between poles = 1,80,000 ÷ 50

⇒ Number of gaps = 3600

⇒ Since both the **starting** and **ending** poles are counted, **Total poles** = Number of gaps + 1

⇒ Total poles = 3600 + 1 = 3601

**∴ The correct answer is 3601.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Linear Arrangement (Pole Counting)

In a straight line, if there are n intervals of equal length, the total number of points (poles/trees) is always n + 1 when both ends are included.

Unit Conversion

To convert Speed from km/h to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert Distance from km to m, multiply by 1000.

Relative Speed

If two objects move in the same direction, relative speed is the difference (S₁ − S₂); if in opposite directions, it is the sum (S₁ + S₂).</p
